what: AR14, AR16 and AR54, the base dressed and spread: where the base's own kit stands on a plot, by the base's level, laid for Stage III's footprints
kit: manifest.json, beside this file: every piece named here is one of its pieces
origin: the middle of the plot's front edge (the edge on the Strip), on the plot's floor
axes: `across` is the plot's own +X, the Breaker's side, to the left as the spawn looks; `along` is studs out of the front edge toward the Strip, so everything on the plot is negative; `turn` is degrees anticlockwise seen from above
toRoblox: in the plot's own frame (WorldService.plot's `at`), Kit.Place(placement, piece, front, floorY) with front = -deep / 2: CFrame.new(across, floorY, front - along) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(turn), 0) * centre. A light the same way, by Kit.Light.

levelMark.note: the level's number on the gate's plate, on both faces (+Y and -Y), in Power's yellow (#FFD23E): the builder's text. The plate stands on two posts over the truss (AR54): out of the gate's view from inside, read whole from the Strip

ground.note: the lot is the plot's own floor under the kit's floors: the deck tile (Base_Deck_Color.png), its Texture's Color3 at `lot`. At 128 the kit's floors cover the plot to its back wall, so it shows only on the Tower's lot behind it, unmarked. The ground is the slab between plots, a flat colour, lifted from #1A1D2E for AR20's C so the open ground beside the crossing isn't black with no haze over it. The Strip and the side street wear the Strip's own paving tile (build/handoff/Strip/maps/Strip_Paving_Color.png, Lantern Row's lifted): stepping off the stones onto the plates is coming home.

standIns.note: until each machine has its model: the boxes in the kit's colours, so nothing on a plot is grey. One steel body for every machine and one accent each; the chambers glow (Neon).

layout.note: AR16 and AR54, the spread: where each thing a player walks to stands, across and in from the front edge (`along` is minus `in`). The floor's pictures are drawn for these places, so a place that moves takes its picture with it. The placement is a star round the generator, which stands at the plot's heart inside a ring of current open toward the gate, with the Breaker and the Door on the two slants toward the gate. Laid again for Stage III (AR54; research's pick and second look, 2026-11-23): the yard is no longer the same on its two sides. The Door's side holds bays 1 and 2, the Training machine and the Forge; the Condenser stands at the back, between the generator and the Breaker; bays 3 and 4 stand outside the Breaker, the battery and the Lab's stone behind it; bays 5 and 6 stay locked at launch, asleep at the back and behind the Door. Each machine was placed by what the game's camera sees of it from the gate. The way in is `avenue` studs wide down the middle line, clear from the gate to the generator. The Breaker's chambers and waiting places keep their offsets from its body, and every machine keeps its turn: a bay's is its placement's (0 on the Door's side, 180 on the Breaker's). What the base will wake stands asleep where it will stand, dark, on a line with no current that lights out to it when it wakes (`sleeping`, `laterBays`). Nothing stands between the gate and the generator. `fit` is the plan's measure at each stage's footprints, taken as BaseFit.Measure takes it on the handoff's own meshes (tools/blender/base_fit.py): the game's Config.World.Fit takes its "128" layout from this table and its Prints from Stage III's.

grounds.note: each place's ground as the floor's pictures draw it, for a prompt or a marker: across from and to, inward from and to. A machine's is its Stage III footprint and 0.9 round it; a bay's and the Lab's stone's is a frame 12.4 square about its spot.

current.note: the conduits drawn in the floor, each from the heart's end outward, across and along: `runs` where the current runs at level 1, `dormant` the casings with none yet (the Lab's and the sleeping bays'). For a pulse of light along each live one, if the builder's effect takes it: a small touch, at research's verdict.

ring.note: the ring round the well: a circle of this radius about the generator, less the quarter that faces the gate. Its current runs from the two links at its sides and the one at its back, toward its open ends.

machines.note: AR15: the machines that have their model, each in place of the builder's stand-in, at every level. Laid as a placement is, raised by `up`. A chamber is its own piece so the builder lights each by its state (EmissiveStrength: full while it breaks a shard, low when empty). A bay's halo is its own piece in one pale swatch: it stands only while a worker works there, in the worker's rarity colour (TR22). The list is level 1's: bays 3 to 6 stand the same way on the yard's lots (`layout.laterBays`, each with its turn). The Festival Door is five pieces and a core: a ring's `spin` is its turn about its own origin, degrees a second, always: CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(spin) * t), so a positive spin goes anticlockwise seen from the mouth (the part's +Z looks out of it).

generatorStages.note: AR67: the Generator's three stages, the swap's table (base_generator.py, `stages`). The Generator takes the stage of the base's ceiling: Stage I at base level 1, II at 2, III at 3 (research, 2026-11-16). A stage's pieces replace the one before's at the same place, laid as a placement is, raised by `up`, turn 0. `moves`: still; turns, about the piece's own upright (`axis` up: Roblox's Y), CFrame.Angles(0, angle * rate, 0) with the core's angle: rate 1 is the core itself, at the plant's speed, and it `breathes` (its size swells that share and back over `period` seconds); the motes follow its angle at their rate, the other way, half as fast; gauge, the step lit while the generation's share reaches it; rises, the collar raised up the column by the demand's share times `studs`. Each stage lists every piece it stands: the motes, the steps and the collar in all three, and Generator2Core in II and III.

battery.note: the battery is a bank: a cell a seat, in this order, as its cap grows with the base's level. The builder lights the cells one after another as the charge rises.

forge.note: AR28: the Forge, the Press, Stage I. Every place here is in the Forge's own frame, turned with it: `across` to its right, `along` toward its front (the Strip), `up` from its floor. ForgeRam stands over the Forge's middle, raised by its underside between `ram`'s heights: rest, the tell's top (the sleeves' foot: never higher) and the contact (on the plate; on an item the builder lays there, that much higher). Its light is the tell: dim at rest, bright as it lifts. The two ForgeGear stand at `gears`, the right one turned half a tooth about its axle so they mesh, and turn opposite ways with the ram: the left anticlockwise seen from the front as it lifts. `degreesPerStud` is the review's rate.

condenser.note: AR28: the Stone Condenser, the Comb, Stage I. Every place here is in the Condenser's own frame, as the Forge's. The comb is the tray: the cups in `cups` fill in their order, a stone or a jewel to a cup, so the comb's lit height is the fill. A cup holding a stone stands CondenserStone at its place, one holding a jewel CondenserJewel, tinted in the jewel type's colour; an empty cup stands nothing. CondenserCore stands at `core` and turns about its own front axis while the Condenser works, still when the tray is full or the power is out.

breakerStages.note: AR32: the Void Breaker's three stages, the Great Jaws, the swap's table. The Breaker takes the stage of its machine level (Config.Base, Stages: 1, 6, 15). Every place is in the Breaker's own frame, turned with it: `across` along the line (chamber 1 nearest the plot's middle, the line going on outward), `along` toward the gate, `up` from its floor. A stage's pieces replace the one before's. `moves`: still; chamber, the chamber of that number, lit by its state as today; while the Breaker hasn't that chamber yet (Config.Base, BreakerChambers: 3 from level 8, 4 from 20), `shut` stands in its place; turns, about the piece's own axle while any chamber breaks, CFrame.Angles(0, 0, angle * sign); waiting, the waiting line's place of that number. `lamp`: where BreakerLamp stands, the crystal's middle.

bayStages.note: AR33: the extraction bays' three stages, the Horned Crown, the swap's table. A bay takes the stage of its own machine level (Config.Base, Stages: 1, 6, 15). Every place is in the bay's own frame, turned with it as Bay is (0 on the plot's left, 180 on its right): `across` toward the outer side's crescent is negative, `along` toward the gate, `up` from its floor. A stage's pieces replace the one before's. `moves`: still; turns, about the piece's own axle while a worker works there, CFrame.Angles(angle * sign, 0, 0). BayHalo and BaySleeping stand as they do at every stage.

batteryStages.note: AR34: the battery's three stages, the Rising Stack, the swap's table. The battery takes the stage of the base's level (Stage I at 1, II at 2, III at 3), and shows that level's cells (Config.Base, Levels.Cells: 2, 4, 8), one on each of its stage's seats. Every place is in the battery's own frame, turn 0: `across`, `along` toward the gate, `up` from its floor. A stage's piece replaces the one before's. `seats` are in the order the cells fill: the bottom tier first, left to right, so the charge climbs. BatteryCell is unchanged; each cell's glow is its share of the charge, as today. This supersedes machines.battery's seats once installed.

trainingStages.note: AR35: the Training machine's three stages, the Weighted Crown, the swap's table. The machine has no level of its own, so it takes the stage of the base's level (Stage I at 1, II at 2, III at 3). Every place is in the machine's own frame, turn 0: `across`, `along` toward the gate, `up` from its floor. The stone (Training) is the same at every stage; a stage's crown replaces the one before's at the same place. `moves`: still; turns, about the crown's own upright while a Voidkin trains, still when none does, at TrainingCrown's rate and sign (Config.World.Grey.Training.Crown). The game picks a piece's axis (Y) and its rate by its Piece being TrainingCrown; TrainingCrown2 and TrainingCrown3 take both.

forgeStages.note: AR36: the Forge's three stages, the Gear Train. It has no level of its own, so it takes the stage of the base's level (Stage I at 1, II at 2, III at 3). Every place is in the Forge's own frame, as machines.forge's. A stage's `frame` stands in place of the one before's; the ram, its poses and the plate are machines.forge's at every stage. A ForgeGear stands at each of `gears`, turned half a tooth about its axle when `turnedHalfTooth` (machines.forge.halfTooth), and turns with the ram at machines.forge.degreesPerStud: `spin` 1 anticlockwise seen from the front as the ram lifts, as Stage I's left gear, -1 the other way, so every gear turns against the ones it meshes.

condenserStages.note: AR36: the Stone Condenser's three stages, the Climbing Comb. It takes its own level: a stage from `fromLevel` (I at 1 to 5, II at 6 to 14, III at 15 and up). Every place is in the Condenser's own frame, as machines.condenser's. A stage's `frame` stands in place of the one before's; the core is machines.condenser's at every stage. `cups` is the stage's tray in its filling order, Stage I's comb and the cups climbing the horns together by height: a stone or a jewel to a cup, as at Stage I, so the lit height is the fill.

baseLevels.note: AR50: what the yard gains at base levels 2 and 3, over level 1's plan. Not a machine: it stands with the base's level (Config.Base), and a level's pieces stand beside those of the level under it, never in their place. Each row is in the plot's frame, laid as a placement is: `across` from its middle line, `along` from its front edge (toward the gate above zero), `up`. `moves`: still; turns, always, about the piece's own axle at `rate` turns a second, the way `sign` gives. A ring stands at its row's place as CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(lean)) * CFrame.Angles(math.rad(tilt), 0, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, angle * sign, 0) in the plot's frame: `tilt` raises its gate side, `lean` dips its right side as seen from the gate, and `axle` is where its axle then points, in Roblox's frame, to check the turn by. LevelFloor, LevelRays, BayWake3 and BayWake4 are light on the deck: no collision, CastShadow off. The fins and the rings are the gate's teal with their light in the mesh's glow, never Neon. The two rings share one axle (the same `tilt`, `lean` and `axle`), through the plot's heart: LevelRing over the floor's second ring and of its size, LevelRingOuter further up it, so its `along` is a little behind the heart's line. Measured against the exported meshes over a full turn (docs/asset-requests.md, AR50, the rings' refit): both pass every stage of the generator and every other piece on the plot by more than 1.2.

bayWake.note: a bay's own piece, stood at the bay's place with the bay's turn while that bay is awake: bay 3 from base level 2, bay 4 from level 3 (AR54: each bay's line runs out to it from the ring, so each has its own; it was one BayWake for both). Bays 5 and 6 stay locked at launch

lighting: the base stands under Lantern Row's dusk: the same sky, ambient, fog and bloom (build/handoff/LanternRow/sky/lighting.json). The conduits, the wall's line and the lamps are drawn for dusk, and under the place's daylight they don't read.
lightsNote: a PointLight over the Breaker's chambers in its violet and one low in the Generator's well in its cyan, the Door's two and the showcase's, Shadows off; everything else that glows is in a glow picture
collision: each piece's `collision` in the manifest; the court's floor and the lines are look only
